oil.summary: Crude surged sharply on Thursday, with WTI +3.1% to $90.85/bbl and Brent +4.1% to $98.46/bbl, as Hormuz risk premiums returned to the fore after Iran's IRGC reported two tankers and a tugboat ablaze in the strait, with headlines framing the incidents as deliberate pressure following the U.S. midterm vote. The supply-disruption bid overshadowed the week's steep sell-off (-10.9% WTI, -14.3% Brent over seven days). Diesel and heating oil outperformed gasoline — HO +3.5% vs. RBOB +1.4% — consistent with reporting that U.S. refineries are structurally pivoting yield toward distillates. The Russian diesel subplot added complexity: tankers reportedly reversed course away from U.S. ports after sanctions pushback from the New Jersey governor and apparent friction with a temporary White House deal to ease Russia oil sanctions. Options markets price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the May 2027 meeting, suggesting the medium-term demand outlook remains cautious even as near-term geopolitical risk keeps a floor under flat price.
drivers: Hormuz incident: IRGC reports two tankers and a tugboat on fire in the strait, lifting geopolitical risk premium across the crude complex
Russian diesel saga: tankers divert away from U.S. ports amid NJ governor sanctions threat and sanctions-wall friction, despite a reported temporary White House easing of Russia oil restrictions
Refinery yield shift: U.S. refiners cutting gasoline output share in favour of diesel/jet fuel, explaining diesel's outperformance of RBOB on the day

gas.summary: Henry Hub edged marginally lower (-0.3%) to $2.95/MMBtu and remains range-bound on the week, reflecting ample domestic supply with no acute demand catalyst. TTF gained 1.8% to €89.64/MWh despite intraday reports of a 2% early-session drop attributed to Democrat midterm gains raising hopes for a U.S.-Iran deal that could ease global supply concerns; the market ultimately pared those losses as the EU moved to rebuff any resumption of Russian gas purchases. The WSJ report of U.S. pressure to restore Russian gas flows via Ukraine sits in direct tension with the EU's stated position of no plans to resume Russian gas imports, leaving the transit-route story unresolved. Hungary's announcement of a full exit from Russian gas by fall 2027 adds a medium-term structural demand shift for alternative supply. Separately, IEEFA data showing $67.8 billion in Asian LNG power projects scrapped or stalled is a bearish medium-term signal for LNG demand from Southeast Asia.
drivers: EU-U.S. divergence on Russian gas: Washington reportedly pushing to restore Russian flows via Ukraine while the EU explicitly rules out resuming Russian gas purchases
Post-midterm Iran deal optimism briefly weighed on TTF intraday before market recovered; geopolitical premium remains in European gas
IEEFA: over half of proposed LNG-to-power projects ($67.8 bn) in key Southeast Asian markets scrapped or stalled, dampening longer-term LNG demand outlook

power.summary: The power and carbon sector offers relatively thin price action today. EU carbon EUAs slipped 1.1% to $84.99/EUA, pulling back modestly despite a solid monthly gain of +4.3%, with no sector-specific headline driving the move. TTF's 1.8% gain is the primary input cost signal for European power generators. On the structural side, two notable demand-side developments emerged: India is set to mandate state utilities to add energy storage capacity to reduce clean-power curtailment, a potentially significant build-out signal for storage markets. Turkey unveiled an ambitious $500 billion energy investment plan to 2040 spanning gas, solar, and nuclear, adding a large long-dated capex story to the regional power landscape. The IEEFA finding of $67.8 billion in stalled Asian LNG power projects is relevant here as a signal that gas-to-power capacity additions in Southeast Asia are slowing materially.
drivers: EU EUA -1.1% on the day despite positive monthly trend; no specific carbon-market catalyst identified in today's headlines
India mandating energy storage additions for state utilities signals accelerating clean-power integration and curtailment-reduction investment
Turkey's $500 bn energy plan to 2040 (gas, solar, nuclear) and IEEFA's $67.8 bn stalled Asian LNG-to-power tally frame divergent regional power investment trajectories
